title: Isolation of Primary Human Colon Tumor Cells from Surgical Tissues and Culturing Them Directly on Soft Elastic Substrates for Traction Cytometry
protocol: Collect the tumor tissue sample right after colon resection.
Transfer the tissue immediately to a 15 ml vial containing 12 ml HBSS solution.
Keep the vial on ice inside an insulated foam box.
Transport the tissue containing vial to a tissue culture hood for further processing within 45 min.
Pour the supplied tissue into a 6 well plate containing 6-7 ml of HBSS solution using a pipette.
Rinse the tissue in HBSS solution twice.
Cut tissue cleanly into separated sections with sterile scissors.
Mince tissue into smaller sections no greater than 1-2 mm³ in size with a sterile scalpel blade.
Weigh a labelled 0.1% trypsin vial (containing 1 ml of 0.1% trypsin solution) before transferring the tissue.
Transfer ~20 mg tissue into each of the 0.1% trypsin vials with a pipette.
Pour ~20 mg tissue and 1 ml trypsin into each well of a 24 well plate.
Put the 24 well plate on shaker in fridge at 4 °C for 16-20 hr.
Prepare polyacrylamide gel substrates and functionalize them with ECM proteins as described in section 3.2.
Transfer tissue from 4 °C trypsin to 4 °C complete growth media vial using a pipette.
Place the tissue containing media vial in a warm water bath at 37 °C for 12-15 min.
Transfer the tissue to a 15 ml vial containing HBSS solution using a pipette.
Shake gently and repeat the transfer step.
Remove tissue from HBSS solution and transfer to 0.1% collagenase solution in HBSS vial containing 1 ml solution.
Incubate for 45 min at 37 °C and 5% CO2 environment in a humidified cell culture incubator.
Warm growth media in a 15 ml vial at 37 °C in water bath during the wait period.
Pull out all tissue fragments into pipette minimizing collagenase carryover.
Eject just the tissue fragments into pre-warmed culture media vials.
Place a 40 µm well-insert filter into each well of a 6 well plate.
Moisten the filter with 1 ml cell culture media.
Triturate tissue in media with a 10 ml glass pipette several times until tissue is completely dissociated.
Deposit the solution onto the filter to remove debris and undissociated parts.
Centrifuge filtered cell suspension in media at 150 x g for 5 min at RT.
Remove the supernatant afterwards.
Resuspend cell pellet with 2 ml fresh culture media.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer (if required).
Seed isolated primary cells on extracellular matrix (ECM) functionalized gels and polystyrene dishes at desired concentration.
Treat glass cover slips with 3-aminopropyltrimethoxysilane (ATS) for 7 min at RT.
Remove the ATS completely with DI water rinse.
Treat cover slips with 0.5% glutaraldehyde solution diluted in PBS from a 70% stock solution for 30 min.
Mix 5% w/v acrylamide solution with 0.05% N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide (bis) solution in 10 mM HEPES-buffered saline to prepare a 2 kPa gel solution.
Use 8% w/v acrylamide and 0.13% N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide (bis) solution in 10 mM HEPES-buffered saline for preparing a 10 kPa gel.
Add ammonium persulfate (10% w/v) at a ratio of 1:200 and N,N,N',N'-tetramethylethylenediamine (TEMED) at a ratio of 1:2,000 to initiate the polymerization process for both gel solutions.
Add 100 µl fluorescent beads to the 2 kPa gel solution as fiduciary markers.
Deposit a drop of 20 μl pre-polymer PA gel solution on a 12 mm² activated glass cover slip.
Place another 12 mm² regular glass cover slip onto the drop, allowing the drop to spread between the cover slips due to capillarity.
Invert the sandwich for 2 kPa gels to ensure that most of the beads come near the cell culture surface.
Cure the PA gel for 45 min at room temperature (RT).
Peel off the top cover slip using a single edge razor, ensuring detachment proceeds from one edge.
Store the cured gels in PBS solution before use.
Incubate substrates with 2 ml pure hydrazine hydrate overnight to functionalize PA gels and glass.
Remove hydrazine hydrate and rinse the substrates thoroughly with deionized (DI) water.
Wash the substrates with 5% acetic acid for 30 min.
Remove acetic acid from substrates.
Rinse substrates thoroughly with DI water.
Immerse substrates in DI water for 30 min.
Incubate substrates with oxidized fibronectin at a concentration of 50 µg/ml for 35 min.
Rinse substrates with PBS on shaker at low rpm for 10 min.
Incubate all substrates at 37 °C in 2-3 ml culture media for 30 min before plating the cells.
Plate cells sparsely (1,000-3,000 cells/cm²) onto each gel-covered glass slip contained in a 35 mm Petri dish.
Allow cells to adhere completely overnight before microscopy.
Warm 0.25% trypsin-EDTA / 10% SDS solution at 37 °C in water bath for 10 minutes before traction experiments start.
Remove one gel from the cell culture incubator and place on the fluorescent inverted microscope stage (32X magnification).
Find a single cell in field of view.
Take a phase contrast image of the cell.
Switch imaging mode to fluorescence and select appropriate filter.
Do not move the microscope stage or sample during this time.
Take an image of the fluorescent beads displaced by cellular traction.
Add 1 ml trypsin/SDS solution to Petri dish to detach the cell from gel.
Do not move the microscope stage or sample during this time.
Also, take a control image of the cell to ensure complete removal from gel.
Take a reference (null force) image of the beads after the cell is removed.
Repeat steps 4.1.2-4.1.8 for all other gels.
Make an image stack using ImageJ from the two images acquired in step 4.1.6 and 4.1.8 for each case.
Use Image → Stacks → Images to Stack after opening the images in ImageJ.
Obtain the displacement field and traction using ImageJ plugins following published methods.
Align the images in the stack using the ‘Template Matching’ plugin.
Use Plugins → Template Matching → Align Slices in Stack → OK after opening the image stack generated in step 4.1.10.
Save the image stack consequently.
Use this new image stack in the following steps.
Obtain the displacement field using the PIV plugin.
Open the image stack saved in step 4.1.11.1.
Use Plugins → PIV → Iterative PIV (Basic) → OK to start PIV analysis.
Accept the PIV and output settings and click OK.
Save the PIV output in the same directory as the original image stack.
Use the FTTC plugin to obtain the traction map.
Plugins → FTTC → Insert material properties, i.e., Young’s modulus and Poisson’s ratio of PA gel → OK.
Select the PIV output file saved in step 4.1.11.2 → OK.
Save FTTC results in the same directory as the image stack and PIV output.
Take the substrates to be immunostained to the laminar hood.
Remove the culture media from the substrates.
Rinse the substrates with PBS.
Fix the cells with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS for 20 min at RT.
Wash the substrates with PBS for 3 times (5 min each time).
Incubate the substrates with 500 µl signal enhancer for 30 min.
Rinse the substrates with PBS.
Incubate cells with monoclonal anti-vinculin antibody at a 1:250 dilution in PBS for 45 min at RT.
Wash the substrates with PBS for 3 times (5 min each time).
Incubate the samples with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 488 goat anti-mouse IgG at a 1:200 dilution in PBS at RT for 30 min.
Wash the substrates with PBS for 3 times (5 min each time).
Incubate cells with TRITC phalloidin conjugates at a concentration of 50 µg/ml for 45 min at room temperature.
Wash the substrates with PBS three times, each wash lasting 5 min.
Image the samples using a confocal scanning laser microscope.
